built_from_inputs_note: This build is identified by a SHA-256 over every input file it read, not by a wall-clock time. Rebuilding from the same inputs produces this same stamp, which is what the CI reproducibility gate checks. The date of any given publication is the git commit date.

questions.q: What does 'opening line' mean in this repository, and how many games have one?
questions.a: 272 side markets and 272 total markets, all in 2021. Every other game has a single undated line. This is a data fact, not a choice.

questions.q: Does the opponent-adjusted model beat the unadjusted one?
questions.a: No. On the holdout the unadjusted estimator scores better on the moneyline (0.06858 vs 0.01117) and both lose on side and total. The adjusted model is not carrying information the naive one lacks.
Out: 0.0% of 10674 player-weeks played (95% CI 0.0%-0.1%); Doubtful: 0.8% of 1684 player-weeks played (95% CI 0.5%-1.4%); Questionable: 63.9% of 14950 player-weeks played (95% CI 63.1%-64.6%)

questions.q: Is the margin/total dependence that supposedly invalidates same-game parlays real?
questions.a: Not in this data. The measured correlation is close to zero and its 95% interval contains zero. The invalid-multiplication rule therefore rests on same-team and same-player dependence, which has NOT been measured here and must not be described as measured.
questions.state: answered — and it corrected a prior assumption

questions.q: Which games could the Week 10 availability capture have informed, given its clock time?
questions.a: 135 of 137 completed games have a pre-kickoff availability vintage. The rest kicked off before the capture existed.

questions.q: What is missing before an injury ablation can be run?
questions.a: A pre-kickoff availability capture per game in the evaluation window. With one capture per week taken after most kickoffs, any ablation would leak the future.
questions.state: answered — it is a scheduling gap

questions.q: Should the leaderboard show staking results next to signal results?
questions.a: It shows both but never combines them. The luck panel exists to show why a staking run cannot be trusted at the sample sizes this project can reach.

questions.q: How many club depth charts are actually verified?
questions.a: 5 of 32. The other 27 are recorded as not acquired, not estimated.

questions.q: Can a starter be identified when the club publishes three players at rank 1?
questions.a: No, and the data says so 25 times. The slot is stored as a group. Choosing one would be an invention.

questions.q: Is there an official depth chart anywhere?
questions.a: No. The nfl.com per-team depth-chart path returns 404. Every chart used is club-published and captioned unofficial.

questions.q: What would make any strategy here eligible to go live?
questions.a: A positive game-cluster lower bound on Brier skill over at least 1,000 prospective games, holding after multiplicity adjustment, plus a defined demotion rule. None is eligible today.

questions.q: Which requirement rows are blocked on a scheduler rather than on analysis?

suggestions.title: Ship the scheduler before anything else
suggestions.why: Rows  are all blocked on the same thing: nothing captures on a cadence. One GitHub Action that runs daily, fetches the official injury report, hashes it and commits closes all of them at once.
options: GitHub Action on a cron schedule (recommended: runs where the network is open)
external cron on a small worker
suggestions.recommendation: GitHub Action. The repository already has workflows; this is the smallest change with the largest unblock.

suggestions.title: Buy one more independent price source
suggestions.why: Every price claim rests on one publisher's files. A second book per game would turn the vig-free decomposition from a single-book calculation into an actual consensus.
options: add a second book's historical closes
keep one book and label it plainly
suggestions.recommendation: Keep one book and label it; only buy a second if the originated line is going to be evaluated against consensus rather than movement.

suggestions.title: Publish the unadjusted model as the headline, not the adjusted one
suggestions.why: The adjusted model does not beat the control. Presenting it first would repeat the pattern every section before this one fell into: a framework that looks sophisticated and loses to a spreadsheet.
options: headline both with the gap column (recommended)
suggestions.recommendation: Headline both, with the gap column, exactly as the brief's 'publish every model total twice' asks.

suggestions.title: Put the blocked-requirement count on the landing page, not in a footnote
suggestions.why: Most requirements are blocked. A landing page that leads with the ones that are done would give a reader a false impression of readiness.
options: counts only on the requirements page
suggestions.recommendation: Count on the landing page. Decision-readiness is the product; shipping it quietly defeats it.

suggestions.title: Treat the depth-chart gap as a purchasing decision, not an engineering one
suggestions.why: 27 clubs remain. Scraping 27 differently-built club pages is weeks of work with a permanent maintenance tail. A licensed structured feed is a contract.
options: license a structured depth/participation feed (cost, stable)
stay at 5 clubs and say so (free, honest, limited)
suggestions.recommendation: License it. The brief already forbids the shortcuts that would make scraping 32 clubs seem cheap.

suggestions.title: Report 'blocked' as a first-class outcome on every page
suggestions.why: The failure mode of this repository's earlier sections was publishing frameworks whose every value was blank, and the failure mode of this one could be publishing numbers whose provenance is thin. A blocked count makes both visible.
suggestions.recommendation: A blocked column, plus the existing Flagged page for the items that need a human read.

status_definitions.done: an artefact exists and a reader can check it
status_definitions.partial: an artefact exists and a named part is missing
status_definitions.blocked: no artefact can be produced from what is held; the gate is named
